findings.evidence: Mathlib/RingTheory/Binomial.lean:277 `noncomputable instance {R} [AddCommMonoid R] [Module ℚ≥0 R] [Pow R ℕ] : BinomialRing R`; Semiconj.lean:138/168 take `[BinomialRing A]` while Commutation.lean:52/61 do not; Kostant/Commutation.lean:59 has to declare a third copy of the same instance to use them.
findings.fix: Add `variable [BinomialRing A]` and delete the local `moduleNNRat` instance, exactly as `TauCeti.ringChoose_mul_pow_eq` (Semiconj.lean:138) already does; consumers then supply their own instance.
findings.issue: `ringChoose_mul_dividedPower_eq` and `dividedPower_mul_ringChoose_eq` take no `[BinomialRing A]` parameter; their `Ring.choose` is elaborated at the `BinomialRing` derived from the file-local `moduleNNRat`. Downstream a consumer with `[Ring A] [Algebra ℚ A]` cannot even state `Ring.choose`, and a consumer whose `BinomialRing A` comes from any other route gets a lemma that does not apply.

findings.evidence: Kostant/Commutation.lean:63 `private theorem mul_ι_eq_ι_mul_add_zsmul_one`; the RHS argument at line 97 is `ι ℚ h + n • (z • (1 : U))`, which does not match the LHS pattern `Ring.choose (ι ℚ h) m` of either theorem.
findings.fix: Expose the ι-level relation publicly (e.g. `ι_mul_ι_eq_ι_mul_add_zsmul_one`), or add a central shift parameter `s` with `Commute s (ι ℚ x)` to both theorems so `Ring.choose (ι ℚ h + s) m` is covered.
findings.issue: The two exported theorems fix the Cartan argument as literally `ι ℚ h`, so they cannot be iterated: after one reordering the argument is `ι ℚ h + n • (z • 1)`, which is not in the image of `ι`, and the relation needed to continue (`mul_ι_eq_ι_mul_add_zsmul_one`) is `private`. PBW normal ordering past several root vectors — the PR's stated consumer use — therefore cannot be done with this API.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean:188 `@[simp] lemma nsmul_eq_mul (n : ℕ) (a : α) : n • a = n * a`; module docstring line 28 says "an integer such as `n z` denotes that integer times the unit of the enveloping algebra".
findings.fix: State the shift as the integer cast the docstring itself describes: `Ring.choose (ι ℚ h + ((n * z : ℤ) : U)) m` (and `- ((n * z : ℤ) : U)` in the dual), at lines 97 and 108.
findings.issue: The weight shift is spelled `n • (z • (1 : U))` (ℕ-smul of a ℤ-smul of `1`), which is not a normal form: `simp` rewrites it to `↑n * ↑z` via `nsmul_eq_mul`/`zsmul_eq_mul`, so a consumer who simps a goal can no longer match the lemma, and iterated shifts never collect.

findings.evidence: Semiconj.lean:47-49 declares the general `R` hypotheses for `smeval_right`; lines 112 and 123 then hard-code `_root_.Polynomial ℤ`, and the proofs (117-119, 128-130) invoke only `smeval_right` and the ℤ-free private shift lemmas.
findings.fix: Generalize both to `{R} [Semiring R] [Module R A] [IsScalarTower R A A] [SMulCommClass R A A] (p : Polynomial R)`; the ℤ instantiation used by `ringChoose_mul_pow_eq` is unaffected.
findings.issue: `smeval_mul_pow_eq` and `pow_mul_smeval_eq` are exported only for `p : Polynomial ℤ`, although the mechanism they wrap (`SemiconjBy.smeval_right`, line 55) is stated for an arbitrary coefficient semiring; nothing in the proofs uses ℤ. A consumer with `Polynomial ℚ` over the same ℚ-algebras this file targets is locked out.

summary: The generic divided-power/binomial lemmas bake their `BinomialRing` instance into the statement via a file-local `Module ℚ≥0 A`, so consumers cannot use them without replicating that instance; and the Kostant-level lemmas cannot be chained past a second root vector because the ι-level relation they need is private.
